name: Mythical Beast
summary: A composite creature of legend joins the parts of several animals into one impossible guardian.
wit: Assembled from spare parts of a dozen nightmares.
artBrief: Ornate open bestiary book seen at an angle with three creature silhouettes rising off its pages (horned head, bat-like wing, curling serpent tail); parchment cream, oxblood leather, teal silhouettes. Book framing keeps it apart from Griffin.

name: Griffin
summary: A lion-bodied, eagle-headed guardian of ancient legend soars with broad feathered wings.
wit: Half king of beasts, half king of birds, fully in charge.
artBrief: Griffin in flight seen from below, wings spread wide in a V, eagle head turned left, lion hind legs trailing; golden tan, white, sky blue.

name: Phoenix
summary: A radiant firebird of legend is reborn from the ashes of its own flames.
wit: Burns out, starts over, looks fantastic doing it.
artBrief: Upright firebird rising from a small ash pile, wings raised in a flame-shaped crown, long curling tail feathers; scarlet, orange, gold. No sun disk (keeps it apart from Bennu/Ra).

name: Kraken
summary: A colossal sea monster of northern legend drags ships beneath the waves with giant tentacles.
wit: Calamari, but it orders you.
artBrief: Giant tentacles rising from a wave line and curling around a tiny tilted sailing ship; deep purple-red tentacles with pale suckers, navy sea.

name: Heracles
summary: The mightiest Greek hero, son of Zeus, wears a lion-skin hood and carries a heavy olive-wood club.
wit: Twelve labours and still no day off.
artBrief: Bust of a bearded muscular hero wearing a tawny lion-head hood over his head, knotted wooden club on shoulder; tawny gold, olive brown, skin tone.

name: Nemean Lion
summary: The invulnerable golden lion of Nemea was the first monster faced in the labours of Heracles.
wit: Arrows bounced off. So did the excuses.
artBrief: Huge golden lion in full-body side view, roaring, with an arrow snapping harmlessly against its shining hide; gold, amber, dark brown mane.

name: Hydra
summary: The many-headed water serpent of Lerna grew two new heads for every one that was cut off.
wit: Cut one off, get two. Terrible negotiating partner.
artBrief: Five serpent necks fanning upward from one coiled body in a marsh pool, each head open-mouthed; swamp green, yellow belly, murky blue water. Different from Jormungandr (single ring) and Medusa (face).

name: Perseus
summary: The Greek hero Perseus used a mirrored shield and winged sandals to defeat the gorgon Medusa.
wit: Never make eye contact. Use the shield.
artBrief: Round polished bronze shield seen front-on reflecting a small snake-haired silhouette, curved sword (harpe) crossing behind; bronze, silver, green.

name: Theseus
summary: The Athenian hero Theseus found his way through the labyrinth by following a red thread.
wit: Navigation tip: always bring string.
artBrief: Young hero in short tunic walking right, holding a ball of red thread that unspools behind him in a long wavy line; red thread dominant, beige tunic, stone grey.

name: Labyrinth
summary: The winding maze built by Daedalus at Knossos was designed so that no one could escape the Minotaur.
wit: Every turn is the wrong one, by design.
artBrief: Top-down square classical meander maze with one entrance and a tiny bull-horn mark at the centre; terracotta walls, sand floor.

name: Daedalus
summary: The legendary Athenian inventor Daedalus designed the labyrinth and crafted wings of feathers and wax.
wit: Brilliant engineer. Terrible at safety briefings.
artBrief: Older bearded craftsman at a workbench binding a single large feather wing with string, compass tool beside; walnut brown, cream feathers, slate.

name: Icarus
summary: Icarus flew too close to the sun on wings of wax and feathers and fell into the sea.
wit: Proof that altitude limits exist for a reason.
artBrief: Small falling figure diagonally top-right to bottom-left, wings shedding loose feathers, large pale sun in upper corner; white feathers, honey wax, warm yellow, light blue.

name: Odysseus
summary: The clever king of Ithaca outwitted a Cyclops on his ten-year voyage home from Troy.
wit: Name's Nobody. Remember that.
artBrief: Bearded hero in a conical pilos cap drawing a great bow, the arrow flying through a row of axe-head rings (the bow contest of Ithaca); bronze, navy tunic, iron grey. No ship (Argo and Charon carry the boat motif).

name: Trojan War
summary: A ten-year siege of Troy united Greek kings against a walled city in the most famous war of legend.
wit: Ten years, one apple, zero chill.
artBrief: High stone city wall with two towers, crossed spears and a round Greek shield leaning in the foreground; sandstone, bronze, crimson.

name: Achilles
summary: The near-invincible Greek warrior Achilles could be wounded only at his heel.
wit: Invincible, terms and conditions apply to the heel.
artBrief: Close-up of a bronze greave and bare heel with a single arrow striking the heel, crest of a helmet in the background; bronze, skin, red crest.

name: Trojan Horse
summary: A giant hollow wooden horse hid Greek warriors and was wheeled into Troy as a false gift.
wit: Never accept a gift that requires a crane.
artBrief: Large wooden horse on a wheeled platform in side view, visible planks, small hatch in its belly; warm wood browns, iron rivets.

name: Prometheus
summary: The Titan Prometheus stole fire from the gods and carried it to humanity in a fennel stalk.
wit: Brought fire to humans. Liver paid the bill.
artBrief: Titan figure striding left holding a hollow stalk with a bright flame at its tip, flame reaching towards a tiny human silhouette; orange flame, grey-blue Titan, green stalk.

name: Pandora's Jar
summary: Pandora's great storage jar released every trouble into the world, leaving only hope inside.
wit: Do not open. Seriously. Ok, hope survived.
artBrief: Large Greek pithos amphora with lid lifting, dark wisps escaping and a tiny bright light remaining inside; terracotta with black meander band, smoky grey, small gold glow.

name: Atlas the Sky-Bearer
summary: The Titan Atlas was condemned to hold up the heavens on his shoulders for eternity.
wit: World's longest shift, no breaks.
artBrief: Kneeling Titan from behind/side supporting a huge star-dotted celestial sphere on his shoulders; dark blue sphere with gold stars, stone-grey figure.

name: Hestia
summary: The gentle Greek goddess of the hearth tends the central flame of every home and temple.
wit: The goddess who keeps the home fires (and peace) burning.
artBrief: Veiled seated goddess in front view holding a shallow bowl with a small flame, round central hearth-stone base; soft peach veil, warm orange, cream. Must differ from Vesta (V82 standing veiled figure before flame): seated, bowl in hands.

name: Helios
summary: The Titan Helios drives the chariot of the sun across the sky every day.
wit: Daily commute: east to west, four fire horses.
artBrief: Golden chariot wheel and two rearing horse silhouettes pulling a blazing sun disk across a gradient sky; gold, orange, light blue.

name: Eros
summary: The winged Greek god of desire shoots golden arrows that make mortals fall in love.
wit: One arrow, instant crush.
artBrief: Young winged youth drawing a bow, gold-tipped arrow aimed right, white wings; pale pink, gold, white. Differs from Cupid by being a slim youth not a chubby infant.

name: Oracle of Delphi
summary: The priestess of Apollo at Delphi spoke prophecies while seated above rising sacred vapours.
wit: Answers guaranteed. Clarity not included.
artBrief: Priestess seated on a tall bronze tripod with swirling vapour rising from a rock cleft beneath; bronze, lavender vapour, white robe.

name: Three Fates
summary: The three Greek Moirai spin, measure and cut the thread of every mortal life.
wit: Spin, measure, snip. No refunds.
artBrief: Single horizontal thread running across the icon: a spindle on the left, measuring rod in the middle, open shears on the right about to cut; golden thread, wood brown, steel.

name: River Styx
summary: The dark river Styx marks the boundary between the world of the living and the Greek underworld.
wit: Swimming not recommended. Ferry only.
artBrief: Winding black-violet river seen from above between grey banks with faint ghostly wisps over the water; black-violet, ash grey, pale green wisps. No gate (V82 Underworld uses an obsidian gate).

name: Charon
summary: The hooded ferryman Charon poles the souls of the dead across the river Styx for a single coin.
wit: Exact change only: one obol.
artBrief: Hooded cloaked ferryman standing at the stern of a narrow boat, holding a long pole, small lantern at the prow; charcoal cloak, dim teal water, yellow lantern.

name: Elysium
summary: The Elysian Fields are the sunlit paradise where Greek heroes rest after death.
wit: Retirement plan for heroes.
artBrief: Rolling green meadow with white asphodel flowers and a single small column under a soft golden sky; meadow green, white, pale gold.

name: Tartarus
summary: The deepest abyss beneath the Greek underworld imprisons the defeated Titans behind bronze gates.
wit: Titans checked in, never checked out.
artBrief: Deep vertical pit seen in cross-section with a chained bronze gate at the bottom and red glow below; black, bronze, ember red.

name: Centaur
summary: A centaur has the upper body of a human joined to the body and legs of a horse.
wit: Twice the legs, half the parking options.
artBrief: Centaur galloping in side view, human torso holding a bow upright, chestnut horse body, no wings; chestnut, skin tone, cream tail.

name: Siren
summary: The sirens of Greek legend sang so sweetly that passing sailors steered onto the rocks.
wit: Great voice. Terrible venue.
artBrief: Bird-bodied siren with a woman's face perched on a sea rock, open beak-like mouth with music swirls drifting out; teal-grey feathers, rock brown, white sea foam. Classical bird form, not a mermaid.

name: Argo
summary: The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece.
wit: Fifty heroes, one boat, endless arguments about rowing.
artBrief: Long Greek galley in side view with a row of oars, painted eye on the prow and a single square sail with a ram emblem; ochre hull, blue eye, cream sail.

name: Ambrosia
summary: Ambrosia is the golden food of the Olympian gods that grants immortality.
wit: One bite and you never need a birthday again.
artBrief: Shallow golden bowl overflowing with glowing honey-gold food, a small dripping ladle beside; gold, honey amber, white sparkle.

name: Cupid
summary: The Roman god of love is shown as a winged child aiming his golden arrows.
wit: Small, winged, and armed with feelings.
artBrief: Chubby winged infant floating with a heart-tipped arrow nocked on a small bow, front view; rosy pink, white wings, gold.

name: Aeneas
summary: The Trojan hero Aeneas escaped burning Troy and became the legendary ancestor of the Romans.
wit: Lost a city, founded a civilisation. Net positive.
artBrief: Warrior carrying an old man on his back and leading a child by the hand, walking away from flames; bronze armour, grey, orange flames.

name: Romulus and Remus
summary: The twin sons of Mars were raised by a she-wolf and went on to found the city of Rome.
wit: Raised by a wolf, founded an empire. Strong parenting.
artBrief: Grey she-wolf in side view standing protectively over two tiny infants beneath her, low Roman hills behind; wolf grey, skin tone, olive.

name: Fortuna
summary: The Roman goddess of luck turns a great wheel that raises and lowers mortal fortunes.
wit: Spin the wheel. Results may vary.
artBrief: Large spoked wheel of fortune with a cornucopia overflowing beside it; gold wheel, green-brown horn, fruit reds.

name: Sol Invictus
summary: The Unconquered Sun was honoured by later Romans with a radiant crown of light.
wit: Unconquered, and very much unclouded.
artBrief: Bust in profile wearing a spiky radiant crown of seven rays, laurel at neck, coin-like circular frame; gold, bronze, warm white. Coin-style profile keeps it different from Helios chariot.

name: Proserpina
summary: The Roman queen of the underworld returns to the surface each spring, bringing the flowers with her.
wit: Half the year in the dark, half in bloom.
artBrief: Young goddess emerging from a crack in the ground holding a bunch of fresh flowers, dark below and green sprouts above; spring green, violet, dark brown.

name: Lares
summary: The Lares were Roman household guardian spirits honoured at a small shrine in every home.
wit: Tiny gods, big opinions about tidiness.
artBrief: Small Roman house shrine (lararium) niche with two little dancing bronze figurines holding drinking horns; terracotta wall, bronze figures, red niche.

name: Cumaean Sibyl
summary: The prophetess of Cumae wrote her oracles on leaves inside a cave of a hundred openings.
wit: Prophecies delivered on leaves. Do not open the window.
artBrief: Dark cave mouth with oak-leaf pages swirling out on a wind, a hooded profile at the edge; dark umber, leaf green, parchment.

name: Huginn and Muninn
summary: Odin's two ravens, Thought and Memory, fly over the world each day and report back to him.
wit: Two ravens, one inbox, full of world news.
artBrief: Two black ravens in flight crossing paths in a circular loop, one larger, against a pale sky; black, slate blue, pale grey. No hat or Odin figure.

name: Mimir's Well
summary: Mimir's well of wisdom lies beneath a root of Yggdrasil, where Odin traded an eye for a drink.
wit: Wisdom on tap. Price: one eye.
artBrief: Round stone well among thick tree roots with a drinking horn resting on its rim and a single glowing eye reflected in the water; mossy grey stone, dark teal water, ivory horn. Explicitly no severed head (avoids modern-game depictions).

name: Norns
summary: The three Norns weave the destinies of gods and humans at the well beneath the world tree.
wit: Past, present and future, carved in one tree trunk.
artBrief: Three hooded figures in a row at a tree base, one carving runes into the trunk, one weaving, one pouring water; dark blue hoods, bark brown, rune cyan.

name: Nidhogg
summary: The dragon Nidhogg gnaws at the deepest roots of the world tree Yggdrasil.
wit: Eats roots. Destroys cosmology. Very rude.
artBrief: Dark winged dragon curled at the bottom of the icon chewing a thick tree root that climbs upward; dark olive dragon, bark brown, bone white teeth.

name: Muspelheim
summary: Muspelheim is the blazing Norse realm of fire, home of the fire giants.
wit: The realm where the thermostat is stuck on 'lava'.
artBrief: Glowing realm sphere/landscape of jagged black rock with rivers of lava and rising sparks; black, molten orange, red.

name: Surtr
summary: The fire giant Surtr guards Muspelheim with a flaming sword destined to set the world ablaze.
wit: Brings a flaming sword to every party.
artBrief: Towering dark giant silhouette with ember cracks across his body raising a long flaming sword; charcoal, ember orange, yellow. Contrast with blue Frost Giant.

name: Svartalfheim
summary: Svartalfheim is the underground Norse realm of master smiths who forged the treasures of the gods.
wit: Underground forges. Best craftsmanship in nine worlds.
artBrief: Cutaway mountain with a glowing forge cave inside, an anvil and small hammer silhouettes at the fire; dark slate, forge orange, rock brown.

name: Draupnir
summary: Odin's golden ring Draupnir drips eight new rings of equal weight every ninth night.
wit: The original compound interest.
artBrief: Thick gold arm-ring in front view with three smaller rings dropping from it in a cascade; gold, deep amber, dark blue background shadow.

name: Brisingamen
summary: The radiant necklace Brisingamen was forged by dwarven smiths for the goddess Freyja.
wit: Four smiths, one necklace, one very determined goddess.
artBrief: Heavy ornate gold necklace laid in a U-shape with amber pendants, centered fiery gem; gold, amber, red.

name: Njord
summary: The Norse god of the sea, wind and fishing is the father of Freyr and Freyja.
wit: Patron of sailors, fishers and everyone who smells like the sea.
artBrief: Bearded sea god wading knee-deep at a shoreline holding up a fishing net full of silver fish, a gull above; sea green, rope beige, silver. No boat.

name: Apples of Idunn
summary: The golden apples kept by the goddess Idunn keep the Norse gods eternally young.
wit: An apple a day keeps Ragnarok... slightly further away.
artBrief: Woven wicker basket holding three shining golden apples with leaves, one apple in front; gold, leaf green, wicker brown.

name: Gjallarhorn
summary: Heimdall's great horn Gjallarhorn will sound across all realms to announce Ragnarok.
wit: The world's loudest alarm clock. Do not snooze.
artBrief: Huge curved horn alone with metal bands and runes, sound waves bursting from its bell to the right; ivory, silver bands, cyan runes. Object only (V82 Heimdall shows the god blowing a horn).

name: Einherjar
summary: The Einherjar are the chosen fallen warriors who feast and train in Valhalla until Ragnarok.
wit: Fight all day, feast all night, repeat until doomsday.
artBrief: Three round Viking shields overlapping in a row with spears and a raised drinking horn above them; red, blue, yellow shields, wood brown.

name: Ymir the First Giant
summary: The primordial giant Ymir was born where the ice of Niflheim met the fire of Muspelheim.
wit: Born from ice meeting fire. Very awkward family reunions.
artBrief: Enormous sleeping giant lying horizontally, half his body frost-blue and half ember-warm, with a tiny cow licking ice at his feet; ice blue, ember orange, grey.

name: Sigurd
summary: The Norse hero Sigurd slew the dragon Fafnir with a reforged sword.
wit: Reforged sword, reformed dragon (it's dead).
artBrief: Young hero raising a long straight sword with a visible repaired notch, round shield on arm, braided hair; steel, forest green, gold.

name: Fafnir
summary: Fafnir was transformed by greed into a great dragon guarding a hoard of cursed gold.
wit: Greed: turns you into a dragon, guaranteed.
artBrief: Wingless serpentine dragon coiled around a pile of gold coins and rings, glaring; dark green, gold, red eye.

name: Ankh
summary: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian hieroglyph for life, carried by gods as a sacred symbol.
wit: The key to eternal life, in loop form.
artBrief: Single large ankh symbol upright, gold with turquoise inlay bands, subtle shadow on sandstone background; gold, turquoise, sand.

name: Khepri
summary: The scarab god Khepri rolls the morning sun into the sky each dawn.
wit: Pushes the sun uphill every morning. Respect.
artBrief: Scarab beetle seen from above pushing a small red sun disk upward, wings slightly open; lapis blue beetle, red-orange sun, gold edges.

name: Bennu
summary: The Bennu is the sacred Egyptian heron of creation and renewal, linked to the sun.
wit: The heron that inspired the phoenix's whole brand.
artBrief: Grey heron with two long crest feathers standing on a tall stone (benben) in profile, not on fire; blue-grey, white, sandstone, small gold sun behind.

name: Sphinx
summary: The sphinx joins a lion's body with a human head as a guardian of Egyptian temples and tombs.
wit: Answer the riddle or wait another thousand years.
artBrief: Reclining sphinx in side view with striped nemes headdress, paws forward, on a desert line; sandstone, blue-gold stripes. Distinct from Pyramid icon: no pyramid in frame.

name: Book of the Dead
summary: The Egyptian Book of the Dead is a papyrus scroll of spells guiding the deceased through the afterlife.
wit: A travel guide for the afterlife. Five stars from the departed.
artBrief: Long unrolled papyrus scroll in a gentle S with hieroglyph rows and a small vignette panel; papyrus beige, black ink, red accents.

name: Ma'at
summary: The Egyptian goddess Ma'at embodies truth, balance and cosmic order, marked by a single ostrich feather.
wit: Truth, order and balance. Also, one excellent feather.
artBrief: Standing goddess in Egyptian profile with one oversized tall white ostrich feather in her headband as the dominant shape, holding a was-scepter; white feather, turquoise, gold. No wings.

name: Weighing of the Heart
summary: In the Egyptian afterlife a heart is weighed against the feather of Ma'at to judge a life.
wit: Light heart: paradise. Heavy heart: snack for Ammit.
artBrief: Large balance scale with a red heart-shaped jar on one pan and a white feather on the other, beam perfectly level; gold scale, red, white.

name: Duat
summary: The Duat is the Egyptian underworld traversed each night by the sun and by the souls of the dead.
wit: Twelve hours of night, twelve gates, zero shortcuts.
artBrief: Star-studded dark blue arch (Nut-like curve) over a narrow underworld river with a row of small gate pylons; midnight blue, gold stars, sand pylons.

name: Solar Barque
summary: Ra's sacred boat carries the sun through the sky by day and the Duat by night.
wit: The sun commutes by boat.
artBrief: Elegant crescent papyrus boat with upturned ends carrying a large gold sun disk in a shrine at its centre, on a thin water line; gold, papyrus green, blue.

name: Nut the Sky Goddess
summary: The Egyptian sky goddess Nut arches her star-covered body over the earth.
wit: Literally holds up the night sky with a backbend.
artBrief: Arched elongated goddess body forming a semicircle over a flat horizon, body covered in gold stars; deep blue, gold, sand horizon.

name: Geb
summary: Geb is the Egyptian god of the earth, often shown reclining green beneath the sky.
wit: The ground floor of Egyptian cosmology.
artBrief: Reclining green-skinned god lying on his side along the bottom of the icon, a goose crown on his head, plants sprouting from his body; leaf green, earth brown, white goose.

name: Canopic Jars
summary: Four canopic jars with animal and human-headed lids preserved organs during mummification.
wit: Four jars, four lids, one very organised afterlife.
artBrief: Row of four short alabaster jars with distinct lids (human, baboon, jackal, falcon); cream alabaster, blue-gold lid details.

name: Cuneiform Tablet
summary: Clay tablets pressed with wedge-shaped cuneiform signs preserve the earliest written stories of Mesopotamia.
wit: The first draft of history, written in mud.
artBrief: Rounded rectangular clay tablet slightly tilted with neat rows of wedge marks and a reed stylus beside it; clay ochre, dark brown wedges, reed tan.

name: Mesopotamian Mythology
summary: The myths of Sumer, Akkad and Babylon tell of creation, floods and the first heroes between two rivers.
wit: Two rivers, a few thousand gods, the first epic.
artBrief: Two wavy blue rivers converging into a V (Tigris and Euphrates) under a gold winged sun disk, reed tufts on the banks; river blue, gold, reed green. No building (Ziggurat owns the tower).

name: Ziggurat
summary: A ziggurat is a massive stepped temple tower of mud brick built to bring the gods closer to earth.
wit: Stairway to heaven, mud-brick edition.
artBrief: Three-tier stepped tower with a central front staircase and a small shrine on top, three-quarter view; sun-baked tan, shadowed brown, blue glazed shrine. Distinct from Pyramid (flat terraces, staircase).

name: Anunnaki
summary: The Anunnaki are the great assembly of Mesopotamian gods who decree the fates of the land.
wit: The original council meeting, minutes in clay.
artBrief: Seven small robed deity silhouettes with horned caps seated in a semicircle council around a central clay tablet, top-down three-quarter view; lapis blue, gold horns, clay ochre.

name: Anu
summary: Anu is the ancient Mesopotamian god of the heavens and father of many gods.
wit: Top of the sky, top of the family tree.
artBrief: Great horned crown floating above a dome of stars, eight-pointed star symbol at centre; lapis blue, gold, white stars.

name: Enki
summary: Enki, god of wisdom and fresh water, is shown with streams of water and fish flowing from his shoulders.
wit: Wise, crafty, and always has a fish on him.
artBrief: Seated bearded god in tiered robe with two streams of water pouring from his shoulders, small fish swimming in them; teal water, gold, beige robe.

name: Inanna
summary: Inanna, queen of heaven, is the Mesopotamian goddess of love, war and the morning star.
wit: Love and war. Usually in that order.
artBrief: Goddess standing on the back of a striding lion, an eight-pointed star shining above her head, holding a ringed staff; deep red, gold star, lion tan. No wings (V82 Isis owns spread wings).

name: Ereshkigal
summary: Ereshkigal rules the Mesopotamian underworld, the land of no return.
wit: Queen of the land of no return. Visiting hours: none.
artBrief: Seated queen on a dark throne inside a low arched gateway descending underground, seven steps below; dark plum, dust grey, dull gold.

name: Babylon
summary: Babylon was the great Mesopotamian city famed for its glazed gates and towering temple.
wit: Big city, bright blue gates, legendary tower.
artBrief: Blue-glazed city gate arch with gold animal reliefs and crenellated towers, front view; cobalt blue, gold, sand.

name: Marduk
summary: Marduk is the patron god of Babylon who defeated the chaos dragon Tiamat.
wit: Babylon's champion, dragon-slayer and city manager.
artBrief: Bearded god in tall horned crown striding right holding a spear-like spade (marru) aloft, a small dragon emblem at his feet; lapis, gold, red.

name: Tiamat
summary: Tiamat is the primordial goddess of the salt sea, imagined as a vast chaos serpent.
wit: Primordial chaos with a very long tail.
artBrief: Single huge sea serpent rising from swirling salt-water spirals, horned head and long wavy body; deep sea green, foam white, purple shadow. One head only, explicitly not a five-headed dragon (avoid tabletop-game design).

name: Lamassu
summary: The lamassu is a winged bull with a human head that guarded Assyrian palace gates.
wit: Bull body, eagle wings, beard on fleek.
artBrief: Stone relief of a winged bull with bearded human head and horned cap in side view, five legs carved; limestone grey, sand, dark blue background.

name: Gilgamesh
summary: Gilgamesh is the legendary king of Uruk whose quest for immortality became the oldest great epic.
wit: Two-thirds god, one-third hero, all ambition.
artBrief: Bearded king in profile with curled beard and hair, holding a small lion under one arm, Assyrian relief style; clay red, black hair, gold. Avoid any modern anime/game design.

name: Humbaba
summary: Humbaba is the monstrous guardian of the Cedar Forest slain by Gilgamesh and Enkidu.
wit: Cedar forest security: monstrous, effective.
artBrief: Grotesque wrinkled lion-like face mask framed by tall cedar trees, face front-on; cedar green, clay orange, dark brown.

name: Epic of Gilgamesh
summary: The Epic of Gilgamesh is one of the oldest surviving works of literature, written on clay tablets.
wit: The world's oldest bestseller. Twelve tablets long.
artBrief: Stack of several clay tablets leaning together like a book set, top one showing a tiny relief of a crowned figure; clay ochre, brown, gold.

name: Tablet of Destinies
summary: The Tablet of Destinies grants whoever holds it supreme authority over the fate of the universe.
wit: Whoever holds it writes the rules.
artBrief: Single glowing clay tablet floating with light rays and a golden wedge-mark star in its centre; clay ochre, radiant gold, deep violet background.

name: Druid
summary: Druids were the learned priests, judges and keepers of lore among the ancient Celtic peoples.
wit: Knows every tree by name, and most of them by gossip.
artBrief: Hooded white-robed figure holding a sprig of mistletoe and a gnarled oak staff; white, oak brown, mistletoe green.

name: Celtic Mythology
summary: The myths of the Irish, Welsh and Gaulish Celts are filled with otherworlds, heroes and shape-shifting gods.
wit: Otherworlds, heroes, and a lot of clever knotwork.
artBrief: Triskele triple spiral in the centre of a round knotwork border; emerald green, bronze, cream.

name: Tuatha De Danann
summary: The Tuatha De Danann are the divine race of Irish myth who arrived in Ireland wrapped in mist.
wit: Arrived in a cloud of mist. Very dramatic entrance.
artBrief: Line of four tall cloaked silhouettes emerging from a bank of mist on green hills, each holding a different treasure (spear, sword, stone, cauldron); misty silver, deep green, gold.

name: The Dagda
summary: The Dagda is the great father god of Irish myth, master of a club, a harp and a cauldron.
wit: Club in one hand, harp in the other, dinner always ready.
artBrief: Burly bearded god in a short cloak holding a huge wooden club resting on his shoulder and a small harp at his hip; earthy brown, green cloak, gold harp.

name: Cauldron of the Dagda
summary: The Dagda's cauldron of plenty never empties and leaves no one hungry.
wit: Bottomless soup. No one leaves hungry.
artBrief: Large round black iron cauldron with knotwork band, steam and overflowing stew, ladle handle sticking out; iron black, bronze band, warm steam white.

name: Lugh
summary: Lugh is the radiant Irish god skilled in every art and wielder of an unstoppable spear.
wit: Master of all crafts. Show-off of most.
artBrief: Young god with a sun-like halo of hair throwing a long fiery-tipped spear diagonally upward; gold, flame orange, green cloak.

name: Brigid
summary: Brigid is the Irish goddess of poetry, healing and the smith's fire.
wit: Poetry, healing and blacksmithing. Overachiever.
artBrief: Woven rush Brigid's cross (four arms around a square centre) with a small flame above; straw gold, flame orange, green background circle.

name: Morrigan
summary: The Morrigan is the Irish goddess of fate and battle who appears as a crow over the field.
wit: Shows up as a crow. You do not want that RSVP.
artBrief: Single black crow perched on a spear shaft, wings half spread, a red moon behind; black, crimson, steel. One crow, distinct from the two-raven Huginn and Muninn icon.

name: Cernunnos
summary: Cernunnos is the antlered Celtic god of wild animals, forests and abundance.
wit: Antlers, torc and the respect of every deer in the forest.
artBrief: Seated cross-legged antlered god holding a gold torc in one hand and a ram-horned serpent in the other, front view; forest green, antler beige, gold.

name: Sidhe Mound
summary: The sidhe mounds are grassy hills where the Tuatha De Danann withdrew into hidden halls.
wit: Looks like a hill. Is actually a party.
artBrief: Round grassy hill with a glowing doorway in its side and a stone kerb ring at the base, starry dusk sky; grass green, soft gold glow, dusk purple.

name: Banshee
summary: The banshee is a spirit woman of the sidhe whose keening wail foretells a death in the family.
wit: Her singing voice is... a warning.
artBrief: Pale long-haired spirit woman with flowing hair and open mouth, wail lines spiralling out, translucent lower body; pale grey-blue, white, dark navy.

name: Tir na nOg
summary: Tir na nOg is the Irish otherworld land of eternal youth across the western sea.
wit: Land of eternal youth. No birthdays allowed.
artBrief: Small green island with a single blossoming apple tree and a golden glow, far across calm sea at sunset; emerald, apple blossom pink, gold, teal.

name: Selkie
summary: Selkies are seal-folk of Celtic and Norse coastal legend who shed their skins to walk on land.
wit: Seal by day, dancer by night. Hides its coat carefully.
artBrief: Grey seal on a rock with its sealskin half pulled back revealing a human hand, sea spray; seal grey, skin tone, sea blue.

name: Cu Chulainn
summary: Cu Chulainn is the great hero of Ulster, son of the god Lugh, who held a ford alone against an army.
wit: One hero, one ford, one very unlucky army.
artBrief: Young hero holding a curved hurley stick and ball, a large grey hound sitting loyally at his side (Cu = hound), red cloak; red, hound grey, wood brown. No spear (Lugh owns the spear throw).

name: Salmon of Knowledge
summary: The Salmon of Knowledge grants all the world's wisdom to the first person who tastes it.
wit: Contains 100% of your daily wisdom.
artBrief: Silver salmon leaping in an arc above a pool beneath hazel branches, hazelnuts falling; silver-pink fish, hazel brown, teal water.

name: Ogham Stone
summary: Ogham stones carry the notched alphabet of early Ireland cut along their edges.
wit: Early Irish text messages, carved in granite.
artBrief: Tall narrow standing stone with notch strokes cut along one vertical edge line (no rune shapes), lichen spots; granite grey, moss green. Distinct from V82 Runestone (blue rune shapes on face).

name: Precambrian Eon
summary: The Precambrian covers nearly nine-tenths of Earth's history, from its formation to the first complex animals.
wit: Four billion years of 'not much happening'. Allegedly.
artBrief: Steaming volcanic coastline under a reddish sky with a thin green-blue microbial film at the water's edge, no animals; rust orange, basalt grey, teal film. Landscape, not a globe (Snowball Earth and Pangaea are globes).

name: Stromatolite
summary: Stromatolites are layered rock mounds built by microbial mats, among the oldest evidence of life.
wit: Earth's first skyscrapers, built by bacteria.
artBrief: Cut-away dome-shaped rock mounds in shallow water showing fine wavy internal layers; tan and cream bands, turquoise water line.

name: Dickinsonia
summary: Dickinsonia is a flat, ribbed Ediacaran organism and one of the earliest known animals.
wit: A living bath mat, 560 million years ahead of fashion.
artBrief: Top-down oval quilted disk with a central groove and many fine ribs, imprinted in sandstone; sandy beige, soft rose, brown shadow.

name: Snowball Earth
summary: During Snowball Earth episodes, ice sheets may have covered almost the entire planet.
wit: The planet went fully frosted. Twice.
artBrief: Whole globe almost completely white and pale blue with tiny dark equatorial strip, cracks in the ice, small black space background; white, ice blue, navy.

name: Ordovician Period
summary: The Ordovician seas filled with reefs, giant nautiloids and early jawless fish.
wit: Seas full, land empty. Beach houses available.
artBrief: Underwater reef of branching bryozoans and honeycomb corals with a small jawless armoured fish swimming over; aqua, coral pink, sand, bronze fish. No cone shell (Orthoceras owns it).

name: Silurian Period
summary: In the Silurian, the first small plants colonised the land while sea scorpions ruled the reefs.
wit: First plants step ashore. Very small steps.
artBrief: Shoreline split view: tiny green forked stems on bare grey rock above, a curved coral reef below the waterline, no animals; grey rock, bright green, coral pink, blue.

name: Devonian Period
summary: The Devonian is the Age of Fishes, when armoured fish thrived and the first forests appeared.
wit: The Age of Fishes. Fins were very in.
artBrief: Murky river delta with an armoured fish shape underwater and early tree silhouettes on the bank; olive water, bronze fish, dark green trees.

name: Permian Period
summary: The Permian saw dry inland deserts on a single supercontinent and sail-backed synapsids.
wit: Desert vibes, sail-backed neighbours.
artBrief: Red desert dunes with a lone scaly conifer, cracked dry ground and a hazy white-hot sun; brick red, ochre, pale yellow. No animal silhouette.

name: Pangaea
summary: Pangaea was the supercontinent that joined almost all of Earth's land into one mass.
wit: All the continents in one group chat.
artBrief: Globe showing a single C-shaped tan-green supercontinent surrounded by one blue ocean, slight latitude lines; ocean blue, land khaki-green.

name: Gondwana
summary: Gondwana was the southern supercontinent that split away from Pangaea and later broke into the southern continents.
wit: South America and Africa used to be very close.
artBrief: Flat map-like view of southern continents fitted together like jigsaw pieces with a visible crack line opening between them; green-tan land pieces, blue gap.

name: Chicxulub Impact
summary: A huge asteroid struck the Yucatan region 66 million years ago, ending the Cretaceous.
wit: Worst. Delivery. Ever.
artBrief: Glowing rock with a fiery trail streaking diagonally down toward a coastline, shockwave arc where it touches; orange-white fire, dark rock, blue-green coast.

name: Mass Extinction
summary: A mass extinction wipes out a large share of Earth's species in a geologically short time.
wit: Nature pressed Ctrl+Alt+Delete.
artBrief: Dark ash-grey landscape with a lone fossil skull half buried and a dim orange sky; ash grey, charcoal, muted orange.

name: Great Dying
summary: The end-Permian Great Dying was the worst extinction in Earth's history, erasing most marine species.
wit: Even worse than the one with the asteroid.
artBrief: Cracked volcanic fissure pouring lava across a barren plain with an empty spiral shell in the foreground; lava red, basalt black, pale shell.

name: Paleogene Period
summary: The Paleogene followed the dinosaurs' extinction, as mammals and birds rapidly diversified.
wit: Dinosaurs out. Mammals: 'Is this seat taken?'
artBrief: Lush tropical forest under a clear sky with a small furry mammal climbing a palm trunk; jungle green, warm brown, light blue.

name: Index Fossil
summary: Index fossils such as trilobites lived for a short, well-known time span and are used to date the rock layers they are found in.
wit: A fossil that doubles as a calendar.
artBrief: Magnifying glass held over a single small trilobite embedded in one highlighted band of a three-band rock chip, with a bracket mark beside that band; magnifier gold rim, slate rock, amber highlight. Focus on the lens, so it differs from V82 Geological Timeline (layer stack) and Trilobite (whole animal).

name: Burgess Shale
summary: The Burgess Shale is a famous Cambrian fossil bed that preserves even soft-bodied animals.
wit: A rock library of weird Cambrian creatures.
artBrief: Dark grey split shale slab with several silvery flattened animal imprints, a geologist hammer leaning on it; slate grey, silver, wood brown.

name: Hallucigenia
summary: Hallucigenia was a tiny Cambrian worm-like animal with paired spines on its back and slender legs below.
wit: Scientists drew it upside down at first. Fair.
artBrief: Side-view tube body with a row of tall paired spines on top and thin tentacle legs below, tiny head; pink-beige body, ivory spines, deep blue water.

name: Opabinia
summary: Opabinia had five stalked eyes and a long flexible nozzle tipped with a grasping claw.
wit: Five eyes, one vacuum-cleaner nose.
artBrief: Segmented swimmer seen from above with five eyes on stalks at the head and a long curling nozzle ending in a claw; rust orange, cream, aqua.

name: Pikaia
summary: Pikaia is a small eel-like Cambrian chordate, an early relative of animals with backbones.
wit: Your great-great-(x10 million) grandparent, maybe.
artBrief: Small translucent ribbon-like swimmer with visible zigzag muscle bands and a faint rod down its length, swimming in an S; pale peach, light blue.

name: Orthoceras
summary: Orthoceras was a straight-shelled nautiloid whose cone-shaped fossils are common in Ordovician rocks.
wit: Like an ammonite, but someone straightened it out.
artBrief: Long straight cone shell pointing diagonally with banded chambers and a squid-like head with short tentacles at the open end; caramel bands, cream, soft pink.

name: Sea Lily
summary: Sea lilies, or crinoids, are stalked animals whose fossil stems form whole beds of limestone.
wit: An animal pretending very hard to be a flower.
artBrief: Tall slender segmented stalk rising from seabed topped by a feathery cup of branching arms; plum purple, cream segments, sea green.

name: Sea Scorpion
summary: Eurypterids, or sea scorpions, were large predatory arthropods of Silurian seas.
wit: A scorpion the size of a person. Swimming. No thanks.
artBrief: Top-down eurypterid with broad paddle legs, spiny front limbs and a long tapered tail spike; rusty brown, amber, sand floor.

name: Cooksonia
summary: Cooksonia was one of the first land plants, a tiny leafless stem forking into spore-bearing tips.
wit: The first lawn on Earth was 3 centimetres tall.
artBrief: Close-up of a few tiny green forked stems with round brown caps at each tip growing from bare wet rock; bright green, brown, grey rock.

name: Archaeopteris
summary: Archaeopteris was a Devonian tree that formed some of the first forests on Earth.
wit: First tree. Invented shade.
artBrief: Single tall straight-trunked tree with layered fern-like flat branches, small for scale ground plants; dark green, bark brown, pale sky.

name: Tiktaalik
summary: Tiktaalik was a Devonian fish with sturdy fins and a neck, a step toward four-legged animals.
wit: Fish with ambitions. Mostly about walking.
artBrief: Flat-headed lobe-finned fish half out of the water, propped on two stout front fins on a muddy bank; olive green, mud brown, blue water.

name: Coelacanth
summary: The coelacanth is a lobe-finned fish lineage from the Devonian, rediscovered alive in 1938.
wit: Declared extinct, then showed up at a fish market.
artBrief: Chunky steel-blue fish in side view with white speckles, fleshy lobed fins and a three-lobed tail; steel blue, white spots, navy.

name: Arthropleura
summary: Arthropleura was a giant millipede-like arthropod over two metres long in Carboniferous forests.
wit: Two metres of legs. Count them if you dare.
artBrief: Giant millipede seen from above coiled into a loose spiral on leaf litter, many tiny legs along the edge; dark red-brown plates, cream legs, forest-floor green. Coil shape avoids the S-curve used by Pikaia and Basilosaurus.

name: Scale Tree
summary: Scale trees like Lepidodendron grew in Carboniferous swamps and their remains formed coal.
wit: Grew fast, died young, became coal.
artBrief: Tall straight trunk with a diamond scale pattern and a forked crown of grass-like leaf tufts above swamp water; olive green, diamond pattern dark green, brown water.

name: Dimetrodon
summary: Dimetrodon was a sail-backed Permian synapsid, more closely related to mammals than to dinosaurs.
wit: Not a dinosaur. Please stop putting it in dinosaur toy sets.
artBrief: Sprawling four-legged reptile-like synapsid side view with a tall rounded spine sail and big toothy head; rust red sail, olive body, sand ground. Sprawling legs and low body distinguish it from bipedal Spinosaurus.

name: Edaphosaurus
summary: Edaphosaurus was a plant-eating sail-backed synapsid whose sail spines carried knobby crossbars.
wit: Same sail, vegetarian menu.
artBrief: Three-quarter top view of a stout small-headed synapsid nibbling a plant, sail with visible crossbar knobs; dusty blue body, cream knobs, green plant.

name: Gorgonops
summary: Gorgonops was a Permian top predator with long sabre-like canine teeth, long before sabre-toothed cats.
wit: Invented sabre teeth 250 million years before the cats.
artBrief: Close-up skull in profile with very long upper canines and a low snout, on a dark rock; bone ivory, charcoal, rust.

name: Lystrosaurus
summary: Lystrosaurus was a stocky tusked mammal relative that survived the Great Dying and spread across Pangaea.
wit: Survived the worst extinction ever by being aggressively average.
artBrief: Squat pig-sized four-legged animal with a short beaked face and two small downward tusks, side view; khaki, cream tusks, brown ground.

name: Diplocaulus
summary: Diplocaulus was a Permian amphibian with a remarkable boomerang-shaped head.
wit: Head shaped like a boomerang. Still came back.
artBrief: Top-down salamander-like body with a wide boomerang/arrowhead-shaped head, swimming; teal-green, yellow belly spots, dark water.

name: Helicoprion
summary: Helicoprion was a Permian shark relative with a spiral whorl of teeth in its lower jaw.
wit: Jaw like a buzz saw, fossil like a cinnamon roll.
artBrief: Large spiral tooth whorl in the centre with serrated triangular teeth spiralling inwards, faint fish outline around; ivory teeth, dark slate, blue.

name: Ginkgo
summary: Ginkgo trees have survived since the age of dinosaurs and still grow today as living fossils.
wit: Outlived the dinosaurs. Still sheds leaves every autumn.
artBrief: Single large fan-shaped ginkgo leaf with a notch in the middle and radiating veins, golden-yellow on green; yellow, green, brown stem.

name: First Flower
summary: Early Cretaceous plants such as Archaefructus were among the first flowering plants.
wit: Flowers arrive. Bees start planning.
artBrief: Simple small pale flower with few petals on a thin water-plant stem rising from a pond, magnolia-like; white-cream, pale yellow, teal water.

name: Petrified Wood
summary: Petrified wood forms when minerals replace a buried tree, turning it to colourful stone.
wit: Wood that became so stressed it turned to stone.
artBrief: Cross-section log slice with rainbow quartz rings and cracked bark edge, lying on sand; amber, red, purple rings, grey bark.

name: Eoraptor
summary: Eoraptor, the 'dawn thief', was one of the earliest known dinosaurs, small and lightly built.
wit: First at the dinosaur party.
artBrief: Small lightly built dinosaur perched on top of a red sandstone boulder, looking back over its shoulder, a low dawn sun disc behind it (the 'dawn thief'); rust red rock, sandy tan body, pale yellow sun. Perched pose + dawn disc keep it apart from V82 Compsognathus.

name: Herrerasaurus
summary: Herrerasaurus was a large early predatory dinosaur from the Triassic of Argentina.
wit: Triassic top dog, back when dinosaurs were the new kids.
artBrief: Early predator lunging diagonally toward the viewer with jaws wide open and long three-fingered hands reaching forward, dark back stripes, ferns at feet; tawny, dark brown stripes, fern green. Head-on lunge, not the V82 side-walk template.

name: Coelophysis
summary: Coelophysis was a slender, fast Triassic theropod known from hundreds of skeletons found together.
wit: Built like a greyhound, ran in gangs.
artBrief: Very slender theropod in mid-leap with both feet off the ground, body stretched horizontally, snapping a small insect from the air with a long narrow snout; olive-tan, rust markings, pale sky. Airborne pose differs from V82 small theropods.

name: Megalosaurus
summary: Megalosaurus was the first dinosaur ever scientifically named, in 1824, from a fossil jaw.
wit: Dinosaur number one, officially.
artBrief: Fossil lower jaw bone in side view with a row of curved blade-like teeth, one replacement tooth emerging, on a museum-label plinth without text; bone ivory, brown, slate. Bespoke because a generic theropod body would duplicate Allosaurus.

name: Majungasaurus
summary: Majungasaurus was a short-armed abelisaurid from Madagascar with a single knob on its skull.
wit: Tiny arms, big attitude, Madagascar address.
artBrief: Head-and-neck portrait in profile of a deep-snouted abelisaur with one rounded forehead knob and rough skull texture, a stubby arm just visible, baobab silhouette behind; plum-grey, cream teeth, baobab brown. Portrait framing differs from V82 Carnotaurus/Ceratosaurus full bodies.

name: Yutyrannus
summary: Yutyrannus was a large early tyrannosaur covered in long filament-like feathers.
wit: Proof that big predators can be fluffy.
artBrief: Large tyrannosaur covered in long shaggy grey-brown feathers standing in falling snow, front three-quarter view with visible breath cloud; grey-brown fluff, white snow, cold blue. Snow setting and shaggy coat differ from V82 Therizinosaurus/Utahraptor.

name: Sinosauropteryx
summary: Sinosauropteryx was the first non-bird dinosaur found with feathers, with a ginger-and-white banded tail.
wit: First feathered dinosaur, and colour-coordinated too.
artBrief: Small fuzzy dinosaur seen from the side with its very long tail curled into a big spiral showing alternating ginger and white bands, dark 'bandit mask' over the eye; ginger, white, leaf green. Tail spiral is the dominant shape.

name: Troodon
summary: Troodon was a small, big-eyed feathered dinosaur with one of the largest brains for its size.
wit: Big eyes, big brain, big plans after dark.
artBrief: Head-and-shoulders close-up of a feathered troodontid with a huge forward-facing amber eye under a crescent moon; mottled brown feathers, amber eye, night blue. Bespoke to avoid duplicating Deinonychus body.

name: Bonebed
summary: A bonebed is a rock layer packed with the jumbled fossil bones of many animals.
wit: Where the herd ended up, all at once.
artBrief: Top-down rock slab crowded with jumbled ribs, vertebrae and a few horn cores at random angles; ochre rock, ivory bones, brown shadows.

name: Mapusaurus
summary: Mapusaurus was a giant South American predator whose bonebed suggests it may have lived in groups.
wit: Giant predator, possibly with a giant friend group.
artBrief: Two overlapping large theropod silhouettes walking together, one adult and one smaller juvenile, low sun behind; dusky red-brown, dark grey, peach sky. Pack composition distinguishes it from Giganotosaurus.

name: Patagotitan
summary: Patagotitan is one of the largest known titanosaurs, with thigh bones taller than a person.
wit: Its thigh bone needs its own room.
artBrief: Enormous upright femur fossil next to a tiny human silhouette for scale, simple museum floor; bone ivory, sandy brown, grey figure.

name: Nigersaurus
summary: Nigersaurus was a short-necked sauropod with a broad straight-edged mouth packed with hundreds of teeth.
wit: Nature's lawnmower, 500 teeth included.
artBrief: Close-up head lowered to the ground with a very wide square vacuum-like mouth lined with tiny teeth, cropping ferns; sage green, ivory teeth, fern green.

name: Supersaurus
summary: Supersaurus was among the longest dinosaurs, a diplodocid with an extremely long neck and tail.
wit: Super long, super sauropod, super name.
artBrief: Extreme horizontal composition: neck and tail run off both edges of the icon (cropped) in one long shallow arc, small body in the centre, tiny conifer for scale underneath; blue-grey body, dark green tree, sand line. Cropped length is the identity cue (V82 sauropods fit inside the frame).

name: Shunosaurus
summary: Shunosaurus was a Jurassic sauropod from China with a small spiked club at the end of its tail.
wit: A sauropod that brought a mace.
artBrief: Short-necked sauropod side view with the tail end curling forward to show a spiked bony club; tan-olive, ivory spikes, brown ground. Needs bespoke: renderer has no sauropod tail club.

name: Mussaurus
summary: Mussaurus, the 'mouse lizard', was first described from tiny hatchlings of an early sauropodomorph.
wit: Named after its baby photos.
artBrief: Tiny big-eyed hatchling sauropodomorph stepping out of a cracked egg, oversized head, long tail; peach-tan baby, cream shell, soft green ground.

name: Ouranosaurus
summary: Ouranosaurus was an iguanodont herbivore from Africa with a tall sail or hump along its back.
wit: Iguanodon body, sail-back accessory pack.
artBrief: Four-legged iguanodont with a tall rectangular back sail, duck-like snout, thumb spike visible; sand yellow body, terracotta sail, green ground.

name: Shantungosaurus
summary: Shantungosaurus was the largest known hadrosaur, a giant duck-billed plant-eater from China.
wit: The biggest duck bill in history.
artBrief: Close-up of a giant duck-billed head in profile with the jaw cut away to show the dense diamond-patterned grinding tooth battery, leaf in the beak; lavender-grey, ivory teeth, leaf green. Head/tooth focus differs from V82 hadrosaur bodies.

name: Torosaurus
summary: Torosaurus had one of the largest skulls of any land animal, with a huge frill pierced by two openings.
wit: The biggest head on land. Hats sold separately.
artBrief: Front three-quarter head view dominated by an enormous wide frill with two large oval windows, two brow horns; olive-tan, rust edge, cream horns. Bespoke: head-focused frill windows.

name: Kosmoceratops
summary: Kosmoceratops had the most ornate skull of any ceratopsian, with a fringe of downward-curling hooks.
wit: Fifteen horns. Absolutely no chill.
artBrief: Front-facing head with a short frill topped by a row of downward-curling hooks like bangs, sideways brow horns; teal-grey, ivory hooks, warm orange accent.

name: Einiosaurus
summary: Einiosaurus was a centrosaurine with a nose horn bent sharply forward like a can opener, known from bonebeds.
wit: Nose horn shaped like a bottle opener.
artBrief: Profile head with a large forward-hooked nose horn and two straight frill spikes, simple background; dusty purple, ivory, sand.

name: Confuciusornis
summary: Confuciusornis was a toothless early bird from China whose males had two long ribbon tail feathers.
wit: First bird with a beak and a fashion statement.
artBrief: Perched crow-sized early bird on a branch with two very long streamer tail feathers hanging down, clawed wing fingers; black-brown, white spots, branch brown.

name: Hesperornis
summary: Hesperornis was a large flightless diving bird with teeth that hunted fish in Cretaceous seas.
wit: Gave up flying. Took up swimming. Kept the teeth.
artBrief: Loon-like diving bird swimming underwater with tiny vestigial wings, toothy beak chasing a fish, bubbles; dark grey-blue, white belly, aqua.

name: Hatzegopteryx
summary: Hatzegopteryx was a robust giant azhdarchid pterosaur that was likely the top predator of its island.
wit: Giraffe-height, walks on its wings, eats dinosaurs.
artBrief: Stocky giant pterosaur walking on all fours with folded wings, massive broad head held low over a small dinosaur silhouette; charcoal brown, pale beak, sunset orange.

name: Pterodaustro
summary: Pterodaustro was a pterosaur with an upturned lower jaw of fine bristle-like teeth for filter feeding.
wit: Basically a flying flamingo with a comb.
artBrief: Pink pterosaur standing in shallow water with a long upward-curving jaw lined with fine bristles; flamingo pink, white, light blue water.

name: Tylosaurus
summary: Tylosaurus was a huge mosasaur with a bony, battering-ram snout.
wit: Uses its face as a battering ram.
artBrief: Mosasaur diving steeply downward with a pointed bony snout tip and fluked tail curling above, bubbles; deep blue-grey, pale belly, ocean gradient. Vertical composition differs from V82 Mosasaurus.

name: Shonisaurus
summary: Shonisaurus was a giant Triassic ichthyosaur as long as a bus.
wit: An ichthyosaur the size of a bus. Please hold on.
artBrief: Huge whale-sized ichthyosaur swimming past a tiny normal fish for scale, small eye, long thin snout; slate blue, white underside, teal.

name: Tanystropheus
summary: Tanystropheus was a Triassic reptile whose stiff neck was longer than the rest of its body.
wit: All neck. Some lizard.
artBrief: Lizard-like body on a shoreline rock with an absurdly long stiff straight neck reaching out over water to snap a fish; olive brown, rock grey, blue.

name: Archelon
summary: Archelon was a giant Cretaceous sea turtle more than four metres long with a leathery shell.
wit: Sea turtle, extra-large, no takeaway lid.
artBrief: Top-down giant sea turtle with ridged leathery shell and huge front flippers; dark teal shell, grey-green flippers, light blue sea.

name: Sarcosuchus
summary: Sarcosuchus was a giant Cretaceous crocodile relative with a long snout ending in a bulbous tip.
wit: The 'SuperCroc'. Tooth count: lots.
artBrief: Top-down giant crocodile with very long narrow snout ending in a round bulla knob, armour scutes on back; olive, dark green scutes, river brown.

name: Deinosuchus
summary: Deinosuchus was a giant alligator relative that ambushed dinosaurs at the water's edge.
wit: Ate dinosaurs for lunch. Literally.
artBrief: Side-view huge alligator head bursting from water with open jaws toward a shoreline, splash; dark grey-green, ivory teeth, brown-blue water.

name: Eohippus
summary: Eohippus, the 'dawn horse', was a dog-sized early horse with several toes on each foot.
wit: Grandfather of horses, the size of a terrier.
artBrief: Small fox-sized horse ancestor in side view with arched back, short neck and multi-toed feet in forest litter; chestnut with pale spots, green ferns.

name: Paraceratherium
summary: Paraceratherium was a hornless giant rhinoceros relative, one of the largest land mammals ever.
wit: A rhino that tried to be a sauropod.
artBrief: Towering hornless long-legged rhino with a long neck browsing leaves from a tree top, side view; warm grey, olive leaves, beige ground.

name: Basilosaurus
summary: Basilosaurus was an early serpent-like whale that was once mistaken for a giant reptile.
wit: A whale named 'king lizard'. Awkward.
artBrief: Very long eel-like whale body undulating across the frame with small front flippers and toothy jaws; blue-grey, white belly, navy sea.

name: Ambulocetus
summary: Ambulocetus, the 'walking whale', was an early whale that could move on land and in water.
wit: Whale with legs. Evolution's beta version.
artBrief: Otter-like furry early whale walking on land at a riverbank on big webbed hind feet, long toothed snout, wet fur; brown fur, pink feet, blue water. Furry body differentiates it from the crocodilians.

name: Doedicurus
summary: Doedicurus was a giant armoured glyptodont with a spiked club at the end of its tail.
wit: Armadillo shell, ankylosaur tail. Accessorised.
artBrief: Dome-shelled armadillo-like giant from rear three-quarter view, tail raised showing a mace-like spiked club; tan shell with hex pattern, dark brown, ivory spikes. Tail club focus distinguishes it from V82 Glyptodon.

name: Cave Lion
summary: The cave lion was a large Ice Age cat painted on cave walls by early humans.
wit: Ice Age king of beasts. No mane, still majestic.
artBrief: Three-quarter head-and-shoulders of a pale maneless lion with faint stripes on a snowy background, normal canines (not sabres); cream-buff fur, amber eye, snow white.

name: Steppe Bison
summary: The steppe bison was a large long-horned Ice Age bison of the mammoth steppe.
wit: Horns like handlebars, coat like a carpet.
artBrief: Side-view heavy humped bison with long sweeping horns and shaggy front, walking on a snowy grass steppe; dark chocolate, cream horns, pale grass.

name: Prehistoric Ape
summary: Early apes of the Miocene lived in forests and include the ancestors of later great apes and humans.
wit: The family tree starts getting very familiar.
artBrief: Small tailless ape hanging by one arm from a forest branch, looking at viewer; reddish-brown fur, leaf green, bark brown.

name: Gigantopithecus
summary: Gigantopithecus was a giant ape of Pleistocene Asia, known mostly from huge fossil teeth and jaws.
wit: Three metres of ape, mostly known from its dental records.
artBrief: Huge dark ape seated in a bamboo grove holding a bamboo stalk, tiny human outline far behind; dark brown-black fur, bamboo green, cream.

name: Australopithecus
summary: Australopithecus walked upright on two legs, as shown by famous fossil footprints in volcanic ash.
wit: Walked upright, kept the eyebrows.
artBrief: Top-down trail of small human footprints across pale volcanic ash running diagonally, a tiny upright figure at the far end; ash grey, warm brown prints, golden grass edge. Footprints dominate; human prints contrast with the V82 three-toed dinosaur track.

name: Homo Habilis
summary: Homo habilis, the 'handy man', is associated with the earliest stone tool industries.
wit: Invented the toolbox. The box was a rock.
artBrief: Crouching hominin striking one stone against another with chips flying, front three-quarter view; brown skin, grey stones, dusty yellow ground.

name: Homo Erectus
summary: Homo erectus was a tall, long-legged human species that spread across Africa and Asia and used fire.
wit: First to go on a really long walk out of Africa.
artBrief: Tall striding human figure in side view carrying a burning torch held high, distant hills; warm brown, flame orange, dusk blue.

name: Neanderthal
summary: Neanderthals were Ice Age humans of Europe and western Asia, skilled toolmakers and hunters.
wit: Big brain, strong brow, great at winter.
artBrief: Profile bust of a Neanderthal with prominent brow ridge, broad nose and a fur hood, snowflakes; warm skin brown, fur grey-brown, ice blue. Dignified, not caricatured.

name: Cro-Magnon
summary: Cro-Magnon is the name for early modern humans of Ice Age Europe, first excavated at a French rock shelter.
wit: Modern humans, Ice Age edition.
artBrief: Front bust of an early modern human wearing a sewn fur parka and a pierced-shell necklace, rock-shelter arch behind; tan fur, shell white, limestone grey.

name: Oldowan Chopper
summary: Oldowan choppers are among the oldest known stone tools, made by knocking flakes from a river cobble.
wit: Version 1.0 of the knife. Very beta.
artBrief: Single rounded grey river cobble with a jagged chipped cutting edge on one side, a few flakes beside it; grey stone, white chip scars, sand.

name: Stone Hand Axe
summary: The teardrop-shaped Acheulean hand axe was the all-purpose tool of Homo erectus for over a million years.
wit: The Swiss Army knife of the Stone Age.
artBrief: Symmetrical teardrop flint hand axe face-on with overlapping flake scars, held at a tilt; honey-brown flint, cream scars, dark outline.

name: Flint Spearhead
summary: Neanderthals hafted sharp flint points onto wooden shafts to make hunting spears.
wit: Sharp idea, well attached.
artBrief: Leaf-shaped knapped flint point bound with sinew cord to the end of a wooden shaft, diagonal; dark grey-black flint, tan sinew, wood brown.

name: Mammoth Hunt
summary: Ice Age hunters worked together with spears to bring down mammoths for meat, hide and bone.
wit: Teamwork makes the mammoth work.
artBrief: Large mammoth silhouette on the right with three small human hunter silhouettes with raised spears on the left, snowy ground; dark brown, black figures, white snow.

name: Mammoth Bone Hut
summary: Ice Age people built dome-shaped shelters from stacked mammoth bones and tusks covered with hides.
wit: Architect's material of choice: leftover mammoth.
artBrief: Dome hut built from interlocking bones and jawbones with two crossed tusks forming an arched entrance, snow; bone ivory, hide brown, snow blue-white.

name: Atlatl
summary: The atlatl, or spear-thrower, let Ice Age hunters hurl darts much farther and faster.
wit: An extra arm, sold separately.
artBrief: Carved wooden spear-thrower with a hooked end holding a long feather-fletched dart, both diagonal, motion lines; wood brown, feather red-white, flint grey.

name: Ochre Hand Stencil
summary: Ice Age artists blew red ochre around their hands to leave stencils on cave walls.
wit: The original 'I was here'.
artBrief: Negative hand outline in sprayed red ochre on a rough beige rock wall, fingers spread; red ochre, beige limestone, brown speckles.

name: Bone Flute
summary: Flutes carved from bird bone and mammoth ivory are among the oldest known musical instruments.
wit: Stone Age playlist: one song, very hollow.
artBrief: Thin hollow bone flute lying diagonally with five round finger holes and a notch, small music notes drifting off; bone ivory, brown holes, soft blue notes.

name: Lion-Man Figurine
summary: The Lion-Man is a 40,000-year-old ivory figure combining a human body with a cave lion's head.
wit: Ice Age sculpture: half lion, half person, all mystery.
artBrief: Small upright ivory statuette with a lion head and human body standing, carved line marks on the arm, on a dark plinth; ivory cream, brown cracks, dark grey.

name: Paleontologist
summary: A paleontologist studies ancient life by finding and interpreting fossils.
wit: Professional dinosaur detective.
artBrief: Kneeling scientist in a wide-brim hat brushing dust from a large fossil claw in rock; khaki, bone ivory, sand.

name: Dinosaur Quarry
summary: A dinosaur quarry is a dig site where fossil bones are exposed layer by layer in the rock.
wit: Dig here. Then dig there. Then for ten more years.
artBrief: Rock face with a grid of string lines over partially exposed bones, a shovel and bucket at the edge; ochre rock, white string, ivory bones.

name: Plaster Field Jacket
summary: Fragile fossils are wrapped in plaster-soaked burlap jackets before being carried from the field.
wit: A cast for a bone that broke 70 million years ago.
artBrief: White rounded plaster-wrapped block with burlap texture, a bone end poking out and a field number painted as abstract marks; white, burlap tan, red marking.

name: Mounted Skeleton
summary: A mounted skeleton assembles fossil bones on a frame to show a prehistoric animal standing as in life.
wit: Back on its feet after 66 million years.
artBrief: Full theropod skeleton standing on a steel armature on a low museum plinth, three-quarter view; bone ivory, steel grey, dark plinth.

name: Coprolite
summary: A coprolite is fossilised dung that reveals what prehistoric animals ate.
wit: Not every fossil is a bone. Some are... worse.
artBrief: Polished coiled brown fossil specimen on a small display stand with a cut face showing bits of bone fragments inside; chestnut brown, amber cut face, grey stand.

name: Gastrolith
summary: Gastroliths are polished stomach stones that some dinosaurs swallowed to help grind food.
wit: Swallowed rocks for digestion. Do not try at home.
artBrief: Small cluster of smooth glossy pebbles inside a faint ribcage outline; glossy grey, rose, ivory rib lines.

name: Fossil Shark Tooth
summary: Fossil shark teeth are among the most common fossils, shed by the thousands over a shark's life.
wit: Sharks lose teeth constantly. Fossil hunters say thanks.
artBrief: Single large triangular serrated fossil tooth held between two fingers for scale, glossy enamel; slate grey-blue enamel, brown root, skin tone.

name: Tar Pit
summary: Asphalt seeps like the La Brea tar pits trapped and preserved thousands of Ice Age animals.
wit: Shiny puddle. Terrible idea.
artBrief: Glossy black pool with bubbles and a sabre-toothed skull and bones sinking at the edge, dry grass around; glossy black, tan, ivory.

name: Feather Impression
summary: Fine-grained limestone can preserve the delicate imprint of individual dinosaur feathers.
wit: A feather, written in stone.
artBrief: Single detailed fossil feather imprint on a cream limestone slab with dendrite stains; cream, warm grey, rust dendrites.

name: Dinosaur Nest
summary: Fossil nests show how dinosaurs arranged their eggs and, in some species, cared for their young.
wit: Good parenting, fossilised.
artBrief: Top-down ring of a dozen elongated eggs arranged in a spiral in a shallow mud mound with a tiny hatchling head peeking; sand, speckled blue-grey eggs, mud brown.
